narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of phospholipids as the major component of plasma membranes.
Explanation of phospholipid structure (phosphate group, fatty acid tails, non-lipid head).
Description of the hydrophobic and hydrophilic properties of the tails and head.
The bilayer's role as a selectively permeable barrier.
Molecules that can pass through the membrane (oxygen, carbon dioxide).
The membrane's significance in creating distinct intracellular and extracellular environments.
